messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV_CACHE_SIZE (prefix-store) anomalous growth detected in prod-us-east-1. metric: kv_cache_keys_total spiked 8.2x over baseline; batch_latency_p95 jumped from 85ms -> 620ms; generation_errors increased to 2.9%. Trigger: anomaly_detector/v2 rule #17.
jamal: taking pager. seeing client pages too. tagging oncall.
jamal: brief context: we pushed a templating change + tokenizer normalization to model-pack 'redwood-open-13b:v4' ~12h ago. suspect prefix hashing mismatch -> cache churn.
amanda: grabbing traces now. firing a quick query against cache keys to see prefix cardinality.
amanda: log snippet from prefix-store (traces):
```
kv_prefix_store.get_keys(prefix_sample=20)
# returns lots of near-duplicates with small whitespace diffs:
"user_prompt:order_summary:customer:1234"
"user_prompt:order_summary: customer:1234"
"user_prompt:order_summary:  customer:1234"
"user_prompt:order_summary:customer: 1234"
# key_count ~ 1.9M -> was ~230k
```
ryan: that matches a tokenizer-normalization mismatch hypothesis. if tokenization differs across runs, the prefix hash will be different; continuous batching tries to cache by the raw template key -> explosion.
priya: I see increased KV write QPS to prefix-store and many small items with TTL not being hit (cache miss rate went up). Also, batching queue latency shows per-batch token spread widened -> poor packing efficiency.
jamal: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable prefix cache (fastest), 2) temporarily reduce continuous-batching window / disable multi-request batching, 3) roll back tokenizer normalization deploy. Which one is fastest to reduce tail latency?
amanda: disabling prefix cache should stop cache churn and reduce writes. batching will still be inefficient but latency should drop. command below to flip in prod control plane:```
# runtime flag flip
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/runtime/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"prefix_cache.enabled": false}'
```
infra-bot: deploy job queued: runtime-config-flip/2050123456 by amanda. CI checks passed. ETA ~ 35s.
clara: support update: two customers (acme-corp, finapps) reported timeouts and 502s to user-facing generate endpoints in the last 20m. CS ticket numbers attached. customers are seeing 10-20s latencies then errors. We should prepare an incident message.
ryan: while that's flipping, throttle batching to limit batch size:```
rdwctl set batching.max_batch_tokens=64 --env=prod-us-east-1
rdwctl set batching.max_concurrent_batches=8 --env=prod-us-east-1
```
jamal: applied both changes in sequence: prefix_cache disabled (infra-bot confirmed), batching throttled. Observing metrics: batch_latency_p95 dropping from 620 -> 210ms in ~3min, error_rate down to 0.6%. KV write QPS dropping by 70%.
priya: good. quick check: are any model variants pinned to different tokenizer builds? need to ensure we don't flip-flop.
amanda: found the root cause: a templating change in service templates-service (PR #4821) replaced a strip-normalize helper that used to call `.strip()` before hashing. new helper left trailing double-spaces in certain render paths. those literal whitespace differences produce distinct prefix keys post-tokenize.
amal: (typo) jamal: copy. who merged PR #4821? looks like ryan did.
ryan: yep that was me, pre-merge we had unit test on strings but missed JS templating path where html-escape + join produced double-space. my bad.
clara: for customer comms: recommend short post: "We discovered increased latencies caused by an internal cache invalidation bug. We've applied a mitigation and are monitoring. Expect follow-up with root cause and timeline." Want me to draft and send?
jamal: yes please draft. include that the fix is applied and we're monitoring; include apology and contact link.
amanda: next steps: 1) roll back template normalization change in templates-service to restore consistent strip behavior, 2) add a runtime-safe normalizer before prefix hashing (idempotent whitespace normalize), 3) add unit + integration tests to prevent tokenizer/templating drift, 4) schedule postmortem.
ryan: I'm pushing a hotfix PR to revert the helper and add the normalizer. pushing commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/templates-service/commit/0a1b2c3 (hotfix/strip-normalizer). CI green. Requesting prod deploy.
infra-bot: deploy templates-service prod-us-east-1 triggered by ryan: deploy/templates-service/prod/2050123468. Canary 5% -> ok.
ryan: after canary looks good, promote to 100%.
jamal: promoting now, promoting to 100%. infra-bot: promotion complete @2050123575.
priya: monitoring shows cache_key_cardinality trending down back towards baseline over ~20min as TTLs expire and normalized keys replace bad ones. batch packing efficiency improving. p95 now ~120ms.
clara: sent initial CS note to affected customers at 2050123600. customers acknowledged, appreciate the quick mitigation.
amanda: creating SEV-2 incident doc and will own postmortem. please add timeline + links.
ryan: short retrospective notes from me: add explicit whitespace-normalization hook in prefix-key generation path (server-side) so templating layers can't break hashing. add lint/test that renders templates and compares pre/post tokenization for stable keys.
jamal: handoff: I'm going offline for the next 2h but will check on updates. Ryan will own the follow-ups. tagging @ryan as incident owner.
ryan: acknowledged. I'll shepherd the postmortem, open follow-up tickets: TICKET-1892 (hotfix revert + normalizer), TICKET-1893 (tests + lint), TICKET-1894 (observability: add key-cardinality alert with adaptive thresholds).
priya: please also add an eval that runs on model-pack changes which asserts prefix-key stability across tokenizer versions.
amanda: agreed. adding to TICKET-1893.
infra-bot: metrics snapshot attached: storage_kv_write_qps: peak 18.2k -> 4.1k after mitigation; batch_latency_p95: peak 620ms -> 110ms after full rollback; generation_error_rate: 2.9% -> 0.2%.
clara: final note: customers re-open if anything else. closing customer comms loop after postmortem. :thumbsup:
jamal: great work team. log this as SEV-2. handoff complete.
ryan: will draft the postmortem and include remediation timeline and deploy links. expected doc ready EOD.
incident-bot: Incident SEV-2 created: INC-2050123456. Links: https://incidents.internal/INC-2050123456
